title: Conditions, Operators, and Boundaries
summary: Write explicit decisions using comparisons, logical operators, if/else, switch, and carefully tested boundaries.
learningObjectives: Explain and apply Conditions, Operators, and Boundaries
Compile and test behavior with warnings enabled
prerequisiteConcepts: Ability to create and save a text file

sections.heading: Core model
sections.content: In C, zero is false and nonzero is true, while relational and logical operators produce 0 or 1. `&&` and `||` short-circuit, which can guard a later expression such as division or pointer access. Assignment `=` and equality `==` are different; enable warnings and place intentional assignments outside conditions. Use `else if` for mutually exclusive ranges and `switch` for discrete integral cases. Every threshold needs tests below, at, and above it. Parenthesize mixed conditions when the intended grouping is not immediately obvious.
